posts.cooked:
We have two physical stores very close together.. within 2 miles. If a customer placed an order we would post as 1 shipment - transferring stock from one location to another to combine.

We noticed recently that customers are being charged for two shipments. How do we stop this?

Shopify only charges a flat shipping rate once across two locations when both locations sit in the same location group inside one shipping profile and use flat or price-based rates.

If your shipping profile uses weight-based or carrier-calculated rates, or if the two stores are in separate location groups under Settings > Shipping and delivery, Shopify calculates a rate for each origin location and adds them together at checkout.

Put both stores in the same location group and use a flat or price-based rate, and the double charge goes away. Right now your customers are being charged for two shipments because the two locations sit in separate location groups, so Shopify adds each location’s rate together instead of charging one. It’s a rate configuration problem, not a packing one, since checkout runs before you combine the stock.

Go to Settings > Shipping and delivery, open the shipping profile that covers these products, then Fulfillment locations, click the second store, choose “Use existing shipping options from another location”, pick the first store and save. Both locations are then in one group and the rate is charged once.

Watch the rate name too, since rates with the same name are added together at checkout even across profiles. One limit: if the rate is weight-based or carrier-calculated, this won’t produce a single charge for an order fulfilled from two locations, because those are calculated per product and the results are combined.
Unfortunately our shipping is weight based, so not working for us.

With weight-based rates, Shopify adds a rate for each location. Turn off “available to fulfill online orders” on the second store, so checkout sees one origin and charges once. Online orders then only use the first store’s stock.
We don’t have the same inventory in both locations - so I need to fulfill from both stores.. otherwise half my stock won’t sell online?

You’re hitting a hard limit: Shopify works out weight-based and carrier rates per fulfilment location and adds them together, and there’s no setting that merges them. So the fix is to let Shopify see one origin while you keep selling both stores’ stock.

Turn off “available to fulfill online orders” at Store B, then move the stock that only sells online from B into Store A’s inventory count with a transfer. Store B keeps its own location for POS, so in-store sales there aren’t affected. You already walk stock between the two to pack orders; this just moves that transfer to before the sale instead of after, and checkout charges one weight-based rate because everything ships from A.

The catch is physical: it only works if you have room at Store A to hold the web-sellable stock. If the ranges overlap a lot, you can leave the shared items at both and only move the B-only lines.

Then the other route is your rates. Swap the weight-based rates for price-based tiers that land close to what you charge now, and put both stores in one location group. Both keep selling online and checkout charges once.

Hi @TVR_UK, keeping both stores’ stock available online is the key requirement here. We can help review your shipping profiles, rates and fulfillment workflow, then assess a setup around how you actually combine shipments. Do you use fixed weight bands or live carrier rates?

Remy | RNR Digital Media Group
This post was flagged by the community and is temporarily hidden.

We have to use weight based shipping as this can vary from 200g to 20kg depending on order. I can’t see why Shopify can’t provide a solution where it adds the order weight and provides the rules set from one location.
Unfortunately we have products that weigh up to 6kg and as little as 3g.

Thanks for clarifying. With that weight range, I can see why you need to keep weight-based shipping.

Have you entered the weight bands and prices yourself in Shopify, or does a carrier calculate the rates? A screenshot of your shipping profile, with any private details hidden, would help me see how the two locations are set up.

Remy | RNR Digital Media Group

Hi @TVR_UK — the distinction is that Shopify calculates the weight-based rate for each shipment, rather than adding all the cart’s weight together and looking it up once in your table. Moving the items between shops after checkout won’t change the shipping charge already calculated.

Putting both locations in the same location group only avoids the duplicate charge for flat rates; that exception doesn’t apply to weight-based rates. Shopify explains that in its combined shipping rates documentation.

Before disabling online fulfilment at the second shop, check the stock impact: inventory held only there would stop contributing to online availability. That workaround needs the stock to be available at the dispatch location before the sale, not just transferred there afterwards.

If keeping both shops’ stock available online and charging by the whole order’s weight are both essential, the shared location group alone won’t meet that requirement.

ai_summary.summarized_text:
The retailer has two nearby stores and combines stock into one parcel after an order, but customers are being charged shipping for both locations. Shopify can charge once when locations share a group and use flat or price-based rates; with weight-based or carrier-calculated rates, it calculates a rate for each fulfillment location and combines them. Moving stock after checkout does not change the rate already charged.

Suggested workarounds are to disable online fulfillment from the second store and make its web-sellable stock available at the first store before orders are placed, or replace weight-based rates with price-based tiers. The first option means stock held only at the second store would no longer contribute to online availability unless transferred in advance. The retailer says weight-based pricing is necessary given the wide range of product weights and wants both stores’ inventory available online.

No solution has been confirmed. The discussion remains open, including whether the rates are manually configured weight bands or carrier-calculated; placing both stores in one location group alone will not resolve the issue for weight-based rates.
